description: Spring's functional endpoints, WebFlux and WebMvc alike: the routes a method that returns a RouterFunction builds with RouterFunctions and RequestPredicates, and with springdoc's SpringdocRouteBuilder.

rules.description: A method declared to return a RouterFunction builds routes with calls. RouterFunctions.route() starts a builder; GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE and OPTIONS on it add a route with a path pattern, an optional request predicate and a handler; route(predicate, handler) and andRoute add one whose path and verb the predicate names (RequestPredicates.GET("/x"), path("/x"), method(HttpMethod.GET), joined with and; accept, contentType and the like narrow a route and name no path). nest(predicate, routes), andNest and the builder's path(pattern, routes) put the routes inside them under the predicate's path, whether they are given as a router function, a Supplier of one (a helper returning Supplier<RouterFunction> is read where it is called) or a consumer of a fresh builder; and, andOther and add join another router function's routes; build makes a router function of what the builder holds at that point; filter, before, after, onError and withAttribute leave them as they are. A builder is one object whatever names hold it, so a route added through a second name is the builder's. A local is read at the value it holds where it is used; one assigned in a branch, with +=, or inside an expression is not read from there on. SpringdocRouteBuilder takes the same calls with an operation consumer last, whose operationId names the operation. A method annotated @Bean is registered by Spring, so its routes are served at the paths they compose; a route-building method of the same class that one calls with no argument is read there, under that caller's prefix; any other one is mounted by code elsewhere, and its paths are relative to a prefix this rule does not know. The handler is a method reference or a lambda that calls one method.
rules.why: halo builds its custom API this way and with no mapping annotation: 75 methods return a RouterFunction, and before this rule not one of the 400 routes its OpenAPI documents declare had a handler; with it 167 do. The Spring PetClinic microservices gateway and the JeecgBoot cloud gateway serve their index page this way. The names are Spring Framework's own (org.springframework.web.reactive.function.server and org.springframework.web.servlet.function: RouterFunctions, RequestPredicates, RouterFunctions.Builder) and springdoc-openapi's (org.springdoc.webflux.core.fn.SpringdocRouteBuilder, org.springdoc.webmvc.core.fn.SpringdocRouteBuilder).

examples.why: a predicate names the verb and the path, accept narrows the route and names neither, and a nest puts what is inside it under its path
WebMvc's builder reads the same; a builder consumer is a fresh builder, a lambda that calls one method names that method, and a filter leaves the routes as they are
springdoc's operation consumer names the operation; a method that is no bean is mounted by the code that calls it, so its paths are relative to a prefix composed elsewhere
a constant of the class is a path its file states; a route-building helper the bean calls is read under the bean's prefix, and is not a set of routes of its own
a path in a variable and a lambda that builds a response itself are said, not guessed; a router function a helper class builds from beans it collects at run time is not read

static resources serve files, not a handler; a local holds the value it was given; a method not declared to return a RouterFunction is not read, whatever it calls, and neither is a List of them, whose members a registry picks at run time
a helper that returns a Supplier of routes hands the nest its routes, and is read there, under the nest's path
the prefix is read where it is used, after it was assigned again; the route added through a second name is the builder's; a local an if may assign is not read, never read at the value it held before
